title: What Is Neurofeedback The Mental Health Treatment Everyone Is Talking About

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 各位心理学家，如果你们能赚到除了用时间换金钱以外的钱，那会怎样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家 Marianne Trent 博士，自 2019 年以来，我一直在开发被动和经常性的收入来源。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有一个令人兴奋的消息。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One-to-Many programme is now open for enrolment.
sentences.zh: Sophie Foote 的“一对多”项目现已开放报名。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the programme myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己曾在 2022 年完成了该项目，此后也支持了两批心理学家走过他们的旅程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的联盟链接加入，你将获得 Sophie 的奖励，以及我提供的独家支持套餐，无需额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalised guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的 WhatsApp 支持、四场小组智囊团会议、大师班、个性化指导、一份 Fortnum and Mason 的礼物，以及限时的一对一辅导奖励。

sentences.en: Enrolment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于 11 月 16 日星期一晚上 10 点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 通过描述中链接的我的奖励页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的奖励。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时为你解答。

sentences.en: What if your brain could learn from its own activity?
sentences.zh: 如果你的大脑能够从自身的活动中学习，会怎样？

sentences.en: Not through talking, not through medication, but through real-time feedback about what it's actually doing.
sentences.zh: 不是通过交谈，也不是通过药物，而是通过关于它实际在做什么的实时反馈。

sentences.en: It sounds futuristic, but it's a technique called neurofeedback.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很科幻，但这是一项被称为神经反馈的技术。

sentences.en: And it's already being used to support people experiencing difficulties with anxiety, attention, trauma, sleep and more.
sentences.zh: 而且它已经被用于支持那些在焦虑、注意力、创伤、睡眠等方面遇到困难的人。

sentences.en: In this episode, counselling psychologist and ILF neurofeedback practitioner, Dr. Madeline Roantree joins me as we explore what neurofeedback actually is, what the evidence says,
sentences.zh: 在这一集中，咨询心理学家兼 ILF 神经反馈从业者 Madeline Roantree 博士加入我，我们将探讨神经反馈到底是什么，证据怎么说，

sentences.en: and whether in future it could play a bigger role in mental health care and treatment.
sentences.zh: 以及未来它是否能在心理健康护理和治疗中发挥更大的作用。

sentences.en: Hope you find it so useful.
sentences.zh: 希望你觉得它很有用。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along to Psychology Actually.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎来到《心理学实际上》（Psychology Actually）。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, a qualified clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是 Marianne Trent 博士，一名合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: And today I am joined by Dr. Madeline Roantree, a qualified counselling psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 今天和我在一起的是 Madeline Roantree 博士，一名合格的咨询心理学家。

sentences.en: Hi, Madeline.
sentences.zh: 你好，Madeline。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: So pleased to have you here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能来这里。

sentences.en: And I'm so excited as well, because today we're talking about something called neurofeedback,
sentences.zh: 我也非常兴奋，因为今天我们要谈论一种叫做神经反馈的东西，

sentences.en: which is something that not that many people have heard of unless they have read the Bessel van der Kolk, The Body Keeps the Score book,
sentences.zh: 除非读过 Bessel van der Kolk 的《身体从未忘记》（The Body Keeps the Score）这本书，否则没多少人听说过它，

sentences.en: which is where both you and I first heard about this from.
sentences.zh: 这也是你和我第一次听说它的地方。

sentences.en: I feel like it's the one that got away from me and it's the pandemic that got in the way of my training.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它是我错过的东西，是疫情阻碍了我的培训。

sentences.en: But you have done it.
sentences.zh: 但你已经做到了。

sentences.en: You are a neurofeedback practitioner.
sentences.zh: 你是一名神经反馈从业者。

sentences.en: Could you tell our audience what neurofeedback is?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我们的听众什么是神经反馈吗？

sentences.en: So neurofeedback is a type of biofeedback.
sentences.zh: 神经反馈是一种生物反馈。

sentences.en: So you might have Fitbits or your aura ring that's picking up your temperature, your heart rate.
sentences.zh: 你可能拥有 Fitbit 或 Oura 戒指，它们会采集你的体温、心率。

sentences.en: Neurofeedback is picking up signals from your brain and feeding that back to you.
sentences.zh: 神经反馈是采集来自你大脑的信号并将其反馈给你。

sentences.en: So you have what's almost subconsciously, really, because your brain is feeding back rather than your sort of conscious self.
sentences.zh: 所以你拥有的是近乎潜意识的东西，真的，因为是大脑在反馈，而不是你的意识层面。

sentences.en: But it's really a sensory feedback on the brainwaves that are going through your mind.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是对你大脑中脑电波的感官反馈。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: And why does that matter and how does that help?
sentences.zh: 那为什么这很重要，它又是如何提供帮助的呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a really good question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: So if we think about when we obviously wake and sleep, we have different states of alertness.
sentences.zh: 如果我们思考当我们清醒和睡眠时，我们有不同的警觉状态。

sentences.en: And so in an ideal world, we want to be alert, but not hypervigilant.
sentences.zh: 在理想的情况下，我们希望保持警觉，但不要过度警觉。

sentences.en: We want to be relaxed, but not disengaged or overly sort of tense and emotionally responsible or responsive.
sentences.zh: 我们希望放松，但不要脱节或过于紧张，并且在情绪上是有反应的。

sentences.en: So we're not sort of shut down.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就不会处于关闭状态。

sentences.en: And in order to be in these states, we have different brainwaves.
sentences.zh: 为了处于这些状态，我们有不同的脑电波。

sentences.en: So there's different frequencies for different brainwaves that sort of when we're awake, for example, we might have theta waves,
sentences.zh: 对于不同的脑电波有不同的频率，例如当我们清醒时，我们可能会有 theta 波，

sentences.en: sort of just daydreaming and hanging out in our heads.
sentences.zh: 就像在做白日梦，在脑子里闲逛。

sentences.en: When we're sleeping, we have predominantly delta brainwaves.
sentences.zh: 当我们睡觉时，我们主要是 delta 脑电波。

sentences.en: When we are sort of focused, we have beta.
sentences.zh: 当我们专注时，我们有 beta 波。

sentences.en: And they have different frequencies.
sentences.zh: 它们有不同的频率。

sentences.en: So these are the different waves that kind of go through our brains in different states of wakefulness, if you will.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是在不同清醒状态下穿过我们大脑的不同波，如果你愿意这样称呼的话。

sentences.en: And when we're particularly anxious and stressed out, we might have high beta waves.
sentences.zh: 当我们特别焦虑和压力大时，我们可能会有高 beta 波。

sentences.en: So these are what we call frequency bands, if you will, with these different frequencies.
sentences.zh: 所以这些就是我们所说的频带，如果你愿意的话，具有这些不同的频率。

sentences.en: So that kind of sort of tells us whether we're awake or asleep in broad terMs.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上告诉了我们是清醒还是睡眠。

sentences.en: Underneath these bands is an infra low frequency.
sentences.zh: 在这些频带之下是一种超低频率。

sentences.en: It's a really slow frequency that is almost like the tidal wave, if you will, sort of how the sort of the undulations of the tide is, as opposed to each wave,
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常缓慢的频率，就像潮汐波一样，如果你愿意的话，就像潮汐的起伏，而不是每一个波浪，

sentences.en: which might be the bands.
sentences.zh: 那可能是指频带。

sentences.en: When we think about the optimal state of being, we want to be alert.
sentences.zh: 当我们思考最佳状态时，我们希望保持警觉。

sentences.en: We want to be awake.
sentences.zh: 我们希望清醒。

sentences.en: We're not only hypervigilant.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅仅是过度警觉。

sentences.en: We want to have this sort of present, relaxed state, but ready to spring into action if we need to be.
sentences.zh: 我们希望拥有这种当下的、放松的状态，但如果需要的话，随时准备采取行动。

sentences.en: And our nervous system is the driving system, if you will, of all of that.
sentences.zh: 而我们的神经系统是这一切的驱动系统，如果你愿意这样说的话。

sentences.en: So whether we are just sort of chilling out and having a cup of tea, but not so chill that if there's something that we need to attend to, like an emergency,
sentences.zh: 所以无论我们只是在放松喝茶，但又不会放松到如果有什么需要注意的事情，比如紧急情况，

sentences.en: that we're not disengaged from that.
sentences.zh: 我们也不会与此脱节。

sentences.en: And we don't want to be so vigilant that we can't relax either.
sentences.zh: 我们也不想太警觉以至于无法放松。

sentences.en: Our nervous system is the system that regulates all of that.
sentences.zh: 我们的神经系统是调节这一切的系统。

sentences.en: And so if our nervous system is out of sync, we will be stuck in different brain states.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们的神经系统不同步，我们就会被困在不同的脑状态中。

sentences.en: And so if our brain can have a feedback information about how it's doing, it can better regulate itself.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们的大脑能得到关于它表现如何的反馈信息，它就能更好地自我调节。

sentences.en: So I don't know if you've done any dancing or yoga or even going to the gym.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是否跳过舞、练过瑜伽甚至去过健身房。

sentences.en: Generally, you'll see there's always mirrors, right?
sentences.zh: 通常，你会看到总是有镜子，对吧？

sentences.en: There's mirrors everywhere in these sorts of scenarios.
sentences.zh: 在这些场景中到处都是镜子。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: So that you can get feedback on your movements.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以得到关于你动作的反馈。

sentences.en: Am I doing this movement correctly?
sentences.zh: 我这个动作做得对吗？

sentences.en: Am I stretching properly?
sentences.zh: 我拉伸得正确吗？

sentences.en: Because if you don't get the feedback, how are you supposed to know to correct yourself?
sentences.zh: 因为如果你得不到反馈，你怎么知道要纠正自己呢？

sentences.en: And this is exactly the same.
sentences.zh: 这完全一样。

sentences.en: So you're feeding back to your brain its own brainwaves so that it can regulate itself.
sentences.zh: 所以你是在把你大脑自己的脑电波反馈给它，以便它能自我调节。

sentences.en: We have this propensity to fix, to get into equilibrium, to get back into harmony, back into sync, because we want to operate functionally, optimally.
sentences.zh: 我们有一种修复、进入平衡、回到和谐、回到同步的倾向，因为我们想要功能性地、最佳地运作。

sentences.en: There's no good being stuck in any of these systeMs.
sentences.zh: 被困在任何这些系统中都没有好处。

sentences.en: So if our brains can get some information about how it's doing, it can then change that.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们的大脑能得到一些关于它表现如何的信息，它就能改变这一点。

sentences.en: That's so interesting.
sentences.zh: 太有趣了。

sentences.en: And, yeah, it's reminded me of the Seben Fisher book I read on neurofeedback.
sentences.zh: 是的，这让我想起了我读过的关于神经反馈的 Seben Fisher 的书。

sentences.en: And I just found it all so fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我发现这一切都太迷人了。

sentences.en: And I think I'm right in saying that she was talking about different brainwaves.
sentences.zh: 我想我没说错，她当时在谈论不同的脑电波。

sentences.en: So, you know, delta, beta, theta, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，delta、beta、theta 之类的。

sentences.en: And also made me think that I'm speaking to you at the moment with a broken hand, which I did watch happen via a mirror.
sentences.zh: 这也让我想起我现在正带着一只骨折的手和你说话，我确实看着它发生，通过镜子。

sentences.en: Because I was at the gym when I did it.
sentences.zh: 因为我受伤时正在健身房。

sentences.en: But can we have a little bit of a look at what might have been going on with my brain since then?
sentences.zh: 但我们能稍微看看从那时起我的大脑可能发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: So I did this on a Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 我是周二做的这件事。

sentences.en: And today is the following Monday.
sentences.zh: 今天是接下来的周一。

sentences.en: So almost a week later.
sentences.zh: 所以差不多一周后。

sentences.en: I have noticed that I am just more exhausted.
sentences.zh: 我注意到我只是更疲惫了。

sentences.en: And I've got less bandwidth for things.
sentences.zh: 我对事情的带宽变小了。

sentences.en: I've had to kind of reprioritize things.
sentences.zh: 我不得不重新安排事情的优先级。

sentences.en: Can we make sense of what's been going on with my brain since that trauma and since the pain?
sentences.zh: 我们能弄清楚自从那次创伤和疼痛以来我的大脑发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对可以。

sentences.en: So I would say that to look at this through a neurofeedback lens, we can see that our nervous systems get impacted by stress.
sentences.zh: 所以我会说，通过神经反馈的视角来看，我们可以看到我们的神经系统会受到压力的影响。

sentences.en: So a physical trauma will be stressful.
sentences.zh: 所以身体创伤会带来压力。

sentences.en: So the pain will presumably affect your sleep, which will then also affect your nervous system and how it operates.
sentences.zh: 所以疼痛大概会影响你的睡眠，这进而也会影响你的神经系统及其运作方式。

sentences.en: And so then we can see how the nervous system kind of gets out of sync, gets out of kilter.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以看到神经系统是如何变得不同步、失去平衡的。

sentences.en: And sometimes it's difficult to get back.
sentences.zh: 有时很难恢复。

sentences.en: So if your nervous system was a little bit more sticky, say, it will take time for it to get back to equilibrium.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你的神经系统稍微有点“粘滞”，比如说，它需要时间才能回到平衡状态。

sentences.en: But that's what healing is.
sentences.zh: 但这正是治愈的意义所在。

sentences.en: Healing is we have this natural propensity to want to heal and get back to equilibrium.
sentences.zh: 治愈就是我们有一种想要治愈并回到平衡的自然倾向。

sentences.en: And so your body is obviously producing extra red blood cells and white blood cells to kind of fix the trauma in your hand.
sentences.zh: 所以你的身体显然正在产生额外的红细胞和白细胞来修复你手上的创伤。

sentences.en: The pain is there to kind of tell you what not to do.
sentences.zh: 疼痛的存在是为了告诉你不要做什么。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Don't don't over don't overwork it.
sentences.zh: 不要过度劳累它。

sentences.en: So otherwise I can't heal.
sentences.zh: 否则我就无法治愈。

sentences.en: So all of that is working perfectly, but it's also taking from your bandwidth.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切都在完美运作，但也占用了你的带宽。

sentences.en: I suppose as long as it's within a window of what you might call reasonable.
sentences.zh: 我想只要它在你可以称之为合理的范围内。

sentences.en: Yeah,
sentences.zh: 是的，

sentences.en: it's reasonable to imagine that you're feeling a little bit tired and a little bit exhausted and maybe a bit frustrated because you can't do the things that you want to do and you have to rearrange stuff.
sentences.zh: 想象一下你感到有点累、有点精疲力竭，也许还有点沮丧，因为你不能做你想做的事情，不得不重新安排事情，这是合理的。

sentences.en: Then you would sort of think about I guess I guess we could maybe use the window of tolerance type of analogy here.
sentences.zh: 然后你会考虑，我想我们可以用“耐受窗口”类型的类比。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That this this is this is to be expected.
sentences.zh: 这是意料之中的。

sentences.en: This is this is understandable.
sentences.zh: 这是可以理解的。

sentences.en: But let's say maybe three weeks later, you're still feeling this and you're still not able to and there's still frustration.
sentences.zh: 但假设三周后，你仍然有这种感觉，仍然无法做到，仍然有沮丧感。

sentences.en: Well, maybe we could then start thinking about maybe the nervous system is stuck in some ways that it needs to be re-regulated.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许我们可以开始考虑神经系统是否在某些方面被困住了，需要重新调节。

sentences.en: And so from a neurofeedback perspective, it can actually help with pain.
sentences.zh: 所以从神经反馈的角度来看，它实际上可以帮助缓解疼痛。

sentences.en: It can help with feeling a sense of calm and reduce the stress, the stress mechanisms that are associated with maybe being tense and in discomfort.
sentences.zh: 它可以帮助产生平静感，并减少与紧张和不适相关的压力机制。

sentences.en: So interesting.
sentences.zh: 太有趣了。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I will keep a mindful watch on that.
sentences.zh: 我会留意的。

sentences.en: I think it's going to be fine.
sentences.zh: 我想会没事的。

sentences.en: I'm already in less pain, so I think it's going to be fine.
sentences.zh: 我已经没那么痛了，所以我想会没事的。

sentences.en: And generally speaking, what sort of presentations can neurofeedback help people to achieve changes in?
sentences.zh: 总的来说，神经反馈可以帮助人们在哪些方面实现改变？

sentences.en: The interesting thing, I think, with neurofeedback.
sentences.zh: 我认为神经反馈有趣的地方在于。

sentences.en: And so what I work with is is infralow neurofeedback, which is slightly different to the band, the one the bands that you were talking about, the alpha, delta, theta.
sentences.zh: 我所做的是超低频神经反馈，这与你谈论的频带（alpha、delta、theta）略有不同。

sentences.en: So those are EEG bands that you can work on.
sentences.zh: 那些是可以处理的 EEG 频带。

sentences.en: I work on the lower frequency, the infralow frequency neurofeedback, which is that sort of this wave, this slow kind of it's almost like the foundation.
sentences.zh: 我处理的是较低频率，超低频神经反馈，这就像是基础。

sentences.en: We sort of talk about the architecture of your nervous system in a way.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是你神经系统的架构。

sentences.en: So once you regulate that and get that where the arousal system is, let's call it imbalance, the instabilities are also balanced out.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦你调节了它，让唤醒系统处于平衡状态，不稳定性也会被平衡掉。

sentences.en: But then it makes sense to add the other band trainings on top of that.
sentences.zh: 但在此基础上增加其他频带训练是有意义的。

sentences.en: So what that means is that that we we we address a broad range of experiences and don't really focus on diagnostics.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们处理广泛的体验，并不真正关注诊断。

sentences.en: So if we were to use diagnostics, say depression or anxiety, those are the sorts of things that neurofeedback can help with.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们使用诊断，比如抑郁或焦虑，这些是神经反馈可以帮助解决的问题。

sentences.en: So autism, ADHD, post-traumatic stress disorder, sleep issues, migraines and headaches, tics, vertigo, perimenopausal symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 所以自闭症、多动症、创伤后应激障碍、睡眠问题、偏头痛和头痛、抽动症、眩晕、围绝经期症状。

sentences.en: So it's because there's downstream effects of regulating a whole network.
sentences.zh: 这是因为调节整个网络有下游效应。

sentences.en: And so then it's an interesting way of working because when I talk, when I work with clients, we have this,
sentences.zh: 这是一种有趣的工作方式，因为当我与客户交谈时，我们有这个，

sentences.en: it's 150 symptom checklist of all of the things that you might experience.
sentences.zh: 这是一个包含 150 个症状的清单，列出了你可能经历的所有事情。

sentences.en: You rate them on a scale from one to ten, how much am I marked by various and you go through psychological, sort of somatic, sort of the, well,
sentences.zh: 你按一到十分的等级对它们进行评分，你经历的各种心理、躯体症状，嗯，

sentences.en: just everything really you can think of from sleep issues to your appetite to everything.
sentences.zh: 真的，你能想到的从睡眠问题到食欲到一切。

sentences.en: And so then you focus on, because that's the way we work around,
sentences.zh: 然后你专注于，因为这就是我们工作的方式，

sentences.en: then you focus on the ones that are scoring the highest because these are the things that are going to be sort of impacted by the moSt.
sentences.zh: 然后你专注于得分最高的那些，因为这些是受影响最严重的。

sentences.en: So it, and it could look like the variability is huge.
sentences.zh: 所以，它看起来变化很大。

sentences.en: So I could have sleep issues, food difficulties, mood issues and distractibility, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我可能有睡眠问题、饮食困难、情绪问题和注意力不集中，对吧？

sentences.en: So it's like a variety of things, which doesn't really necessarily fall under a particular diagnostic.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像各种各样的事情，并不一定属于特定的诊断。

sentences.en: Yet with the neurofeedback, we're having some ideas around, okay, this is, this might be an issue with instability, say.
sentences.zh: 然而通过神经反馈，我们有一些想法，比如，好吧，这可能是不稳定性的问题。

sentences.en: There's instability in my system that I, my system struggles to toggle easily back and forwards to get to equilibrium.
sentences.zh: 我的系统存在不稳定性，我的系统很难轻松地来回切换以达到平衡。

sentences.en: Or it could be an arousal issue that I have too much of something or too little of something.
sentences.zh: 或者也可能是唤醒水平的问题，比如我体内某种物质过多或过少。

sentences.en: So I might have, if I have an over arousal system, then it's anxiety, panic attacks, you know, those, those sorts of things, sort of insomnia, racing thoughts.
sentences.zh: 如果我的唤醒系统处于过度唤醒状态，就会出现焦虑、恐慌发作，你知道的，诸如此类的问题，还有失眠、思绪纷乱等。

sentences.en: That's sort of an over arousal.
sentences.zh: 这算是一种过度唤醒。

sentences.en: So then I'm having some ideas around, okay, what, what is it that the nervous system needs?
sentences.zh: 所以我开始思考，神经系统到底需要什么？

sentences.en: It needs to have a sort of a calmer, or it could be an under arousal.
sentences.zh: 它需要平静下来，或者也可能是唤醒不足。

sentences.en: So you have low mood, lethargy, fatigue, brain fog, these sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 比如情绪低落、嗜睡、疲劳、脑雾等等。

sentences.en: So that's a low arousal.
sentences.zh: 这就是唤醒不足。

sentences.en: And so, so it's kind of like an arousal and instability question that we target from an ILF neurofeedback perspective.
sentences.zh: 所以，从ILF神经反馈的角度来看，我们针对的就是这种唤醒水平和不稳定性问题。

sentences.en: The downstream effects of that is these huge sort of broad range of difficulties, I guess, that people experience.
sentences.zh: 我想，由此产生的下游影响就是人们所经历的各种各样的困难。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: So with, I know when I was reading the literature, it's about, you know, for example, complex trauma.
sentences.zh: 我读过相关文献，比如关于复杂性创伤的。

sentences.en: And you've got an over arousal because the body and the mind is constantly trying to work out why it's not safe or to feel safe or to kind of manipulate that environment.
sentences.zh: 你会处于过度唤醒状态，因为身心一直在试图弄清楚为什么不安全，或者试图让自己感到安全，又或者试图去操纵周围的环境。

sentences.en: And they might be more anxious, they might be lower in mood.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会更焦虑，或者情绪更低落。

sentences.en: And so how might you expect, I don't know, I don't know how many sessions you typically have for somebody with a complex trauma background,
sentences.zh: 那么你觉得，我不知道，对于有复杂性创伤背景的人，通常需要多少次疗程，

sentences.en: but how might that person's presentation change over time if they were treated with neurofeedback?
sentences.zh: 但如果他们接受神经反馈治疗，他们的表现会随时间发生怎样的变化？

sentences.en: So with, with PTSD, for example, you would, this is the thing is that's, that's a, that's a diagnostic.
sentences.zh: 以创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）为例，这属于诊断范畴。

sentences.en: So we'd, from a, from a neurofeedback perspective, you would kind of like ask other questions you'd want to have sort of more,
sentences.zh: 从神经反馈的角度来看，你会提出更多的问题，你想要了解更多信息，

sentences.en: well, I suppose you would do this anyway within trauma work, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想在创伤治疗中你本来也会这样做，对吧？

sentences.en: You'd want to have a full, the whole biopsychosocial kind of template to ask about.
sentences.zh: 你会想要一个完整的生物-心理-社会模型来作为询问的基础。

sentences.en: But you'd also ask specifically, which I suppose, let me show you, I've got, you have sensors, I'm going to deviate slightly.
sentences.zh: 但你也会问一些具体的问题，我想，让我给你展示一下，我有传感器，稍微偏离一下主题。

sentences.en: You have sensors that you, that will pick up, that you put on different places.
sentences.zh: 你有传感器，可以拾取信号，你需要把它们放在不同的位置。

sentences.en: So with infra-low frequency, you have four sensors that you sort of place, but two of them always get placed in different places,
sentences.zh: 对于红外低频（ILF）神经反馈，你需要放置四个传感器，但其中两个总是根据你想处理的问题放置在不同的位置。

sentences.en: depending on what it is that you want to work with.
sentences.zh: 这取决于你想解决什么问题。

sentences.en: So you'd ask a whole bunch of questions in terms of figuring out where to start.
sentences.zh: 所以你会问一堆问题来确定从哪里开始。

sentences.en: Is it instability?
sentences.zh: 是稳定性问题吗？

sentences.en: Do I want to stabilize the system?
sentences.zh: 我是想稳定这个系统吗？

sentences.en: So headaches, seizures, flashbacks, dissociation is an instability issue, say.
sentences.zh: 比如头痛、癫痫、闪回、解离，这些都是不稳定性问题。

sentences.en: If, for example, somebody with PTSD has flashbacks, this would be what we call a T3, T4 instability issue.
sentences.zh: 如果PTSD患者出现闪回，这通常就是我们所说的T3、T4不稳定性问题。

sentences.en: So I put a placement on my, just above my ears, on the left and the right-hand side.
sentences.zh: 所以我会在耳朵上方，左右两侧各放一个传感器。

sentences.en: If it's more sort of anxiety and panic, that's an intrusive thought, say, then I would want to lower the arousal,
sentences.zh: 如果是焦虑和恐慌，比如侵入性思维，那么我就想降低唤醒水平，

sentences.en: where then I'd put the placements at the back on the right-hand side and just above the right ear.
sentences.zh: 这时我会把传感器放在右后侧和右耳上方。

sentences.en: So those are the two main placements that you would start to sort of stabilize and regulate the nervous system.
sentences.zh: 这就是你开始稳定和调节神经系统的两个主要放置位置。

sentences.en: And so, again, it depends on what the client is coming with in terms of what is the most significant difficulty or experience that they're having.
sentences.zh: 同样，这取决于客户带着什么问题来，以及他们所经历的最严重的困难或体验是什么。

sentences.en: I suppose the thing with diagnostics is it kind of gives you a rough idea about where in the department store that you're going to go shopping in a way, right?
sentences.zh: 我想诊断的意义在于，它让你大致知道要去百货公司的哪个部门购物，对吧？

sentences.en: If it's depression, it's more likely to be low arousal, brain fog, low motivation.
sentences.zh: 如果是抑郁症，更有可能是唤醒不足、脑雾、动力不足。

sentences.en: So then you have some ideas about the protocols, where you want to place them.
sentences.zh: 这样你对方案和放置位置就有了一些想法。

sentences.en: If it's anxiety, you want to figure out, is it rumination, overthinking, OCD-like, or is it more sort of visceral kind of in the body, sort of panic versions?
sentences.zh: 如果是焦虑症，你需要弄清楚是反刍思维、过度思考、强迫症倾向，还是更偏向于身体上的恐慌感？

sentences.en: So, again, it will kind of tell you whether you want to, if it's an instability or an arousal question.
sentences.zh: 所以，这会告诉你这到底是稳定性问题还是唤醒水平问题。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: And so these are electrodes that get placed actually onto the scalp or the forehead.
sentences.zh: 这些电极实际上是贴在头皮或前额上的。

sentences.en: And I think I'm right in saying that you kind of almost like playing games.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，这就像是在玩游戏。

sentences.en: So I think I remember there was one case where you've got two rockets and you need to kind of think, think the rocket's taking off.
sentences.zh: 我记得有个案例，屏幕上有两枚火箭，你需要通过思考让火箭起飞。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: How does it work?
sentences.zh: 它是如何运作的？

sentences.en: So those are the band frequencies.
sentences.zh: 那些是频带频率。

sentences.en: So the C-Burn book doesn't talk about INF, neurofeedback.
sentences.zh: C-Burn的书里没有提到ILF神经反馈。

sentences.en: So the band frequency, so the typical ones that you would train are alpha, alpha-theta or alpha-beta.
sentences.zh: 频带频率，通常训练的是Alpha波、Alpha-Theta波或Alpha-Beta波。

sentences.en: And they can work on operant conditioning.
sentences.zh: 它们可以通过操作性条件反射来起作用。

sentences.en: So you have some kind of a reward, so like a rocket that sort of takes off or what have you.
sentences.zh: 你会得到某种奖励，比如火箭起飞之类的。

sentences.en: With infra-low frequency, the frequency is so slow, there's no kind of reward for the brain necessarily.
sentences.zh: 而红外低频的频率非常慢，大脑不一定会有那种奖励机制。

sentences.en: And so what the feedback looks like, depending on the program that you're using, it could be, well, there's three ways of getting the feedback.
sentences.zh: 根据你使用的程序，反馈的形式可能不同，获取反馈的方式有三种。

sentences.en: So visually, so you might be looking at a screen.
sentences.zh: 视觉上，你可能在看屏幕。

sentences.en: And the screen, depending on what you're using, I mean, you could use, for example, a YouTube.
sentences.zh: 屏幕上的内容取决于你使用的软件，比如你可以用YouTube。

sentences.en: So you can add YouTube onto the system and then it would increase or decrease in size, for example.
sentences.zh: 你可以把YouTube视频接入系统，然后视频的大小会随之增大或减小。

sentences.en: So that, what would you call that, sort of the frequency by which it decreases and increases is kind of like a pulse, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 这种减小和增大的频率，就像是一种脉冲。

sentences.en: And that pulse is letting the brain know that this is what your frequency is doing.
sentences.zh: 这个脉冲在告诉大脑：这就是你目前的频率状态。

sentences.en: This is what your brain is doing at these particular electrode placements.
sentences.zh: 这就是你的大脑在这些特定电极位置下的活动情况。

sentences.en: Now, nothing's going into the brain.
sentences.zh: 没有任何东西进入大脑。

sentences.en: A lot of people worry about something's happening to them because they sound like, you know, electrodes sound quite, so I call them sensors because that's all they're doing.
sentences.zh: 很多人担心会有什么东西作用于他们，因为“电极”听起来很吓人，所以我称它们为传感器，因为它们的功能仅此而已。

sentences.en: They're just picking up information and then giving it back to you, a bit like an aura ring or a Fitbit.
sentences.zh: 它们只是拾取信息并反馈给你，就像Oura戒指或Fitbit手环一样。

sentences.en: Nothing's happening to you.
sentences.zh: 没有任何东西作用于你。

sentences.en: All it is is your brain kind of realising that this pattern that is being shown to me is mine.
sentences.zh: 它只是让你的大脑意识到：原来这个呈现给我的模式是我自己的。

sentences.en: So I think an example could be you and I might have a conversation, you know, in a networking event and then you'll hear your name and you'll sort of turn, you'll react to that.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，你和我可能在社交活动中交谈，当你听到自己的名字时，你会转头，你会做出反应。

sentences.en: You're not talking to me, listening purposely out for your name being called.
sentences.zh: 你并不是在跟我说话时特意去听有没有人叫你的名字。

sentences.en: Your brain is doing that.
sentences.zh: 这是你的大脑在自动处理。

sentences.en: Our brains scan for patterns the whole time.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑一直在扫描模式。

sentences.en: If I was to say Mary Mary had a little, your brain is instantly going to go lamb, right?
sentences.zh: 如果我说“玛丽，玛丽有一个小……”，你的大脑会立刻接上“羊羔”，对吧？

sentences.en: Because that's the pattern it's learned.
sentences.zh: 因为这是它学到的模式。

sentences.en: So our brains are constantly looking for patterns.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的大脑一直在寻找模式。

sentences.en: So now you're looking at this screen and you have headphones on so you're also getting auditory information and I also have a tactile one so it's like a little box that sort of vibrates.
sentences.zh: 现在你看着屏幕，戴着耳机，所以你也在接收听觉信息，我还有一个触觉反馈装置，就像一个小盒子会震动。

sentences.en: So I've got three methods by which my brain can then give me feedback on its rhythMs.
sentences.zh: 所以我大脑可以通过这三种方式获得关于其节律的反馈。

sentences.en: And so that's what it's doing is noticing these patterns and thinking, oh gosh, this is me, this is me.
sentences.zh: 它所做的就是注意到这些模式，然后想：噢，天哪，这是我，这是我。

sentences.en: And then, hang on a second, this doesn't feel really nice.
sentences.zh: 然后，等等，这种感觉不太舒服。

sentences.en: And so then it regulates itself.
sentences.zh: 于是它就会自我调节。

sentences.en: It's really clever.
sentences.zh: 这真的很聪明。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And it's also a lot to almost get your head around as well, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 而且对于没听说过的人来说，这也很难理解，不是吗？

sentences.en: Like if someone's never heard of this.
sentences.zh: 如果有人从未听说过这个。

sentences.en: It's very passive.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常被动的过程。

sentences.en: As a therapist,
sentences.zh: 作为治疗师，

sentences.en: you're asking questions and you're noticing micro movements in the face and you're kind of like listening out for stuff that's not said and you're sort of really active.
sentences.zh: 你通常会问问题，观察面部细微动作，倾听言外之意，你是非常主动的。

sentences.en: But here you're just watching something and listening to something.
sentences.zh: 但在这里，你只是在看和听。

sentences.en: And then as a practitioner, I'm sort of asking my clients, how does it feel on the body?
sentences.zh: 作为从业者，我会问客户：身体感觉如何？

sentences.en: How are you feeling?
sentences.zh: 你感觉怎么样？

sentences.en: And kind of using their feedback to inform me on whether we're on the right track or not.
sentences.zh: 并利用他们的反馈来判断我们是否走在正确的轨道上。

sentences.en: Hi there, only me.
sentences.zh: 嗨，是我。

sentences.zh: 我插播一下，告诉大家一个好消息，因为我真心认为关于神经反馈的讨论早就该进行了。

sentences.zh: 如果你像我一样，对神经反馈如何改变心理健康感到着迷，那么你正在听正确的对话。

sentences.en: Okay, so for example, autistic people, people with an ADHD diagnosis, what kind of changes might they see?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么例如，自闭症患者、被诊断为多动症（ADHD）的人，他们可能会看到什么样的变化？

sentences.en: And is it okay that we're making those changes or helping people to make those changes?
sentences.zh: 我们做出这些改变或帮助人们做出这些改变，这样做合适吗？

sentences.en: So certainly from social psychiatry back in the day when I worked in that, we always talked about whether symptoms were bothersome.
sentences.zh: 当然，从我过去从事社会精神病学的经验来看，我们总是讨论症状是否令人困扰。

sentences.en: So the example would be OCD, for example.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，强迫症（OCD）。

sentences.en: So let's say I have OCD and I check my door handle five times every morning before I leave.
sentences.zh: 假设我有强迫症，每天早上出门前都要检查五次门把手。

sentences.en: Now, does that bother me?
sentences.zh: 现在，这困扰我吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Is it an issue?
sentences.zh: 这是一个问题吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Do I need to have therapy for it?
sentences.zh: 我需要为此接受治疗吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不需要。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Or as my CBT trainer once said, you know, I know when I'm stressed, I'm going to be really pissed off if my husband hasn't put his cup away in the dishwasher.
sentences.zh: 或者正如我的CBT导师曾经说过的，我知道当我压力大时，如果我丈夫没把杯子放进洗碗机，我会非常生气。

sentences.en: So do I want to have therapy about that?
sentences.zh: 所以我需要为此接受治疗吗？

sentences.en: No, because I know what it's all about.
sentences.zh: 不需要，因为我知道这是怎么回事。

sentences.en: So it's kind of like the same sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这其实是同样的事情。

sentences.en: Like, are you bothered by these things?
sentences.zh: 比如，这些事情困扰你吗？

sentences.en: So my son, for example, he's seven and school reports came back with, you know, he doesn't listen, he's distractible, he keeps playing with his other friends and he doesn't,
sentences.zh: 以我七岁的儿子为例，学校报告说他不听讲、容易分心、总是和朋友玩闹，而且他……

sentences.en: you know, and this is not unusual for us.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这对我们来说并不罕见。

sentences.en: It's no big news for us because it's like, for the umpteenth time, can you do X?
sentences.zh: 这对我们来说不是什么大新闻，因为就像是第无数次问他：你能做某事吗？

sentences.en: And even in swimming, you'd see him like doing all sorts of other things rather than listening to the instructor.
sentences.zh: 即使在游泳课上，你也会看到他做各种其他事情，而不是听教练指导。

sentences.en: So clearly an inattention issue.
sentences.zh: 所以这显然是一个注意力不集中的问题。

sentences.en: And so I tried the infralone neurofeedback on him in a half term and you're always sort of, is it neurofeedback or is it placebo?
sentences.zh: 我在期中假期间尝试在他身上使用红外低频神经反馈，你总是会怀疑：这是神经反馈的作用还是安慰剂效应？

sentences.en: Like, is it just because we are doing this?
sentences.zh: 是因为我们正在做这件事吗？

sentences.en: You know, and I said to my husband, well, the proof will be in the pudding if the school recognises anything.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我对我丈夫说，如果学校能看出什么变化，那才是真正的证明。

sentences.en: And sure enough, I think two weeks later we have, you know, a parent meeting and the teacher goes quite spontaneously.
sentences.zh: 果然，我想两周后我们开家长会时，老师非常自发地说了出来。

sentences.en: It's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: Since the half term, he's been so good.
sentences.zh: 期中假之后，他表现得太好了。

sentences.en: And you're just like, well, okay, fine.
sentences.zh: 你只会觉得，好吧，行吧。

sentences.en: You know, and I was like really curious, like me, the scientist in me was kind of like, so, because they have these tracker systems, you know, if they misbehave or do something,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我当时真的很好奇，我内心作为科学家的那一面在想，因为他们有追踪系统，如果学生表现不好或做了什么，

sentences.en: they go on tracker and there's a warning system.
sentences.zh: 他们会被记录在追踪系统里，还有一个警告系统。

sentences.en: And I'm like, so, and she goes, he hasn't been on tracker, he hasn't been on tracker all week.
sentences.zh: 我问她，她说：他这周没有被记录，整周都没有。

sentences.en: And I'm like, oh, so how often would be on tracker before half term?
sentences.zh: 我说：噢，那期中假之前他多久会被记录一次？

sentences.en: And she goes, oh, about four or five times a week.
sentences.zh: 她说：噢，大约每周四五次。

sentences.en: And now I go, she goes, oh, or maybe once or twice.
sentences.zh: 现在呢？她说：噢，可能只有一两次。

sentences.en: I'm like, okay, right, we've got hard data here that suggests there's something that's changing.
sentences.zh: 我说：好吧，我们有确凿的数据表明确实发生了变化。

sentences.en: And it's kind of like blind control in a way because she doesn't know what we've been doing.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上就像盲控实验，因为她不知道我们一直在做什么。

sentences.en: So you could say, well, it's good to be distractible if you're looking out for danger, say.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，如果你需要防范危险，分心是有好处的。

sentences.en: But if you're in a school environment and need to concentrate and listen to what the teacher is saying, well, then that's obviously not a really productive position to be in.
sentences.zh: 但如果你在学校环境里，需要集中注意力听老师讲课，那显然不是一个高效的状态。

sentences.en: And plus the poor kid, right, he's getting an 80% reduction in being told off, really, right?
sentences.zh: 而且可怜的孩子，他被训斥的次数减少了80%，对吧？

sentences.en: So school is now going to be a much nicer experience.
sentences.zh: 所以学校现在对他来说会是一个更愉快的体验。

sentences.en: And at home, you know, it's now, can you get ready for school?
sentences.zh: 在家里，现在是：你能准备好去上学吗？

sentences.en: And he's sandwiched in hand that he's made by himself with clothing and book bag ready and shoes.
sentences.zh: 他自己做好了三明治，衣服、书包和鞋子都准备好了。

sentences.en: And I'm like, who are you?
sentences.zh: 我当时想：你是谁？

sentences.en: Like, who are you, right?
sentences.zh: 你是谁，对吧？

sentences.en: So massive changes.
sentences.zh: 所以变化是巨大的。

sentences.en: It's really impressive.
sentences.zh: 这真的令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: Yeah, it sounds it.
sentences.zh: 是的，听起来确实如此。

sentences.en: I think I could go on that for myself.
sentences.zh: 我想我也想亲自尝试一下。

sentences.en: I think my husband would like me to do it as well.
sentences.zh: 我想我丈夫也会希望我去做这件事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Is there much emerging evidence base?
sentences.zh: 目前有足够的证据基础吗？

sentences.en: So, of course, when I was in the NHS, I said, oh, can we, you know, can you pay for me to be trained in this?
sentences.zh: 当然，当我在英国国家医疗服务体系（NHS）工作时，我说，哦，我们能不能，你知道，你能资助我接受这方面的培训吗？

sentences.en: And they were like, no.
sentences.zh: 他们的回答是，不行。

sentences.en: So I was going to be self-funding.
sentences.zh: 所以我打算自费。

sentences.en: But is there any emerging stuff?
sentences.zh: 但现在有什么新的研究进展吗？

sentences.en: Is it ever going to end up on the NICE guidance, could you imagine?
sentences.zh: 你能想象它最终会被纳入英国国家卫生与临床优化研究所（NICE）的指导方针吗？

sentences.en: Definitely, definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对会，绝对会。

sentences.en: I think it's headed in that direction.
sentences.zh: 我认为它正朝着那个方向发展。

sentences.en: There was a massive study, a literature review that came out in 2022 that found, they found 18 studies that they could use, basically, out of, I think,
sentences.zh: 2022年发布了一项大规模研究，是一篇文献综述，他们发现了18项可以使用的研究，基本上，在他们确定的，我想，

sentences.en: 36 or about 40 pieces of work that they had identified as for infralow of Eurofeedback specifically.
sentences.zh: 36或40篇左右专门针对红外低频神经反馈（Infralow Neurofeedback）的研究中。

sentences.en: But they'd also demonstrated a sort of an almost an exponential growth in research around the area since, I think, the last 20 years.
sentences.zh: 但他们也展示了，我想在过去20年里，该领域的研究几乎呈指数级增长。

sentences.en: I mean, neurofeedback has been around for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，神经反馈已经存在很长时间了。

sentences.en: Infralow has been around for a shorter amount of time.
sentences.zh: 而红外低频神经反馈出现的时间较短。

sentences.en: So the active treatment group, I suppose they range, well, a lot of the studies are single case studies.
sentences.zh: 所以主动治疗组，我想他们的范围，嗯，很多研究都是单例研究。

sentences.en: And I think one or two of the studies had maybe 40 participants in them, and maybe half of those were control groups.
sentences.zh: 我想其中一两项研究可能有40名参与者，其中可能有一半是对照组。

sentences.en: So the main criticism is we don't have big enough controls.
sentences.zh: 所以主要的批评是我们的对照组规模不够大。

sentences.en: Another difficulty, I think, is that it's very individualized.
sentences.zh: 我认为另一个困难是它非常个性化。

sentences.en: You know, our nervous systems are different depending on what environment we've grown up in.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们的神经系统根据我们成长的环境而有所不同。

sentences.en: You know, you've just broken your hand, say, so maybe your nervous system is out of kink a little bit.
sentences.zh: 你知道，比如你刚摔断了手，所以你的神经系统可能有点失调。

sentences.en: And so it's quite individualized in terms of the placements, whether it's, you know, over the ears or behind the head or wherever we put these placements,
sentences.zh: 因此，在放置位置方面非常个性化，无论是，你知道，在耳朵上方还是在脑后，或者无论我们把这些电极放在哪里，

sentences.en: which makes it difficult to standardize as terms of protocols, right?
sentences.zh: 这使得在协议方面很难标准化，对吧？

sentences.en: So those are the main criticisms of it.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是主要的批评意见。

sentences.en: That said, there's just recently, I think it was this year, that was an MFRI study published with single ILF sessions and neurological changes already in a single session.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，就在最近，我想是今年，发表了一项功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）研究，涉及单次红外低频（ILF）疗程，仅一次疗程就产生了神经学变化。

sentences.en: So there's definitely promising research that's coming out and more people are, it's having, you know, if you think about medicine, it takes decades for even in, I think,
sentences.zh: 所以确实有很有希望的研究正在出现，而且更多的人正在，它正在，你知道，如果你考虑医学，它需要几十年，甚至在，我想，

sentences.en: I think the average age in medical school
sentences.zh: 我想医学院的平均年龄

sentences.en: for some finding in the medical field, it takes 17 years on average for it to reach medical school to be taught to our GPs or whoever, right?
sentences.zh: 对于医学领域的某些发现，平均需要17年才能进入医学院，传授给我们的全科医生或其他人，对吧？

sentences.en: So it's, you know, this is a, in some, in one way, it's the brand new thing, even though it's decades old, but it's definitely gaining traction.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这在某种程度上是一个全新的事物，尽管它已经有几十年的历史了，但它肯定正在获得关注。

sentences.en: And the changes that I've seen is, I sometimes tell myself, like, why is this not more widely available?
sentences.zh: 我所看到的改变是，我有时会问自己，为什么这没有得到更广泛的应用？

sentences.en: It's that transformative, I find.
sentences.zh: 我发现它就是这么具有变革性。

sentences.en: Since Dr. Madeleine and I chatted, I had a little dive into the research for neurofeedback.
sentences.zh: 自从我和Madeleine博士聊天后，我稍微深入研究了一下神经反馈的研究。

sentences.en: And I also got in contact with Bmedic, who gave me a few more examples of relevant research.
sentences.zh: 我还联系了Bmedic，他们给了我一些更相关的研究案例。

sentences.en: I know that if you're a fan of the show, you also care about research.
sentences.zh: 我知道如果你是这个节目的粉丝，你也关心研究。

sentences.en: So since Dr. Madeleine and I chatted, I have had a little look into the evidence base even more, and I've chatted with Bmedic as well.
sentences.zh: 所以自从我和Madeleine博士聊天后，我更深入地研究了证据基础，也和Bmedic聊过了。

sentences.en: The neurophysiological effects of neurofeedback are actually now coming together as a pretty solid evidence base.
sentences.zh: 神经反馈的神经生理学效应实际上现在已经汇集成了一个相当扎实的证据基础。

sentences.en: There's also the landmark fMRI study, which was published in the journal NeuroImage, and looking at the kind of connections in the brain as a result of ILF neurofeedback.
sentences.zh: 还有那项具有里程碑意义的fMRI研究，发表在《NeuroImage》杂志上，研究了ILF神经反馈对大脑连接的影响。

sentences.en: All of the details for this are in the show notes and in the description for the video.
sentences.zh: 所有这些细节都在节目笔记和视频描述中。

sentences.en: Hope that you also think this really matters and it's making you even more excited.
sentences.zh: 希望你也认为这真的很重要，并且让你更加兴奋。

sentences.en: Now, back to Dr. Madeleine and myself.
sentences.zh: 现在，回到我和Madeleine博士的对话。

sentences.en: It's such a beautiful bolt-on to therapy.
sentences.zh: 它是治疗中一个非常好的补充。

sentences.en: So I'm beginning to see this as sort of neurofeedback is like working on the hardware and therapy works on the software.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始认为神经反馈就像是在处理硬件，而治疗是在处理软件。

sentences.en: We're like updating our thoughts and our belief systems, but the neurofeedback just gets us over the edge in terms of the finish line with our therapeutic goals.
sentences.zh: 我们就像是在更新我们的思想和信念系统，但神经反馈只是在我们的治疗目标方面帮我们跨过终点线。

sentences.en: It's really fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这真的很迷人。

sentences.en: It's like the treatment that reaches parts of the brain and the presentation that other therapies can't, it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 听起来这就像是一种能够触及大脑其他疗法无法触及部位的治疗方法。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: One hundred percent.
sentences.zh: 百分之百。

sentences.en: And in terms of, you know, medication can have side effects.
sentences.zh: 而且关于，你知道，药物可能会有副作用。

sentences.en: Are there any risks to this?
sentences.zh: 这有什么风险吗？

sentences.en: That's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题。

sentences.en: So yes and no.
sentences.zh: 所以，既是也不是。

sentences.en: So there's no, it's not side effects as such.
sentences.zh: 所以没有，它本身不是副作用。

sentences.en: It's just the effect of training a system, nervous system.
sentences.zh: 这只是训练神经系统的效果。

sentences.en: So if you, if you are already hypervigilant, say, and you have a frequency that's a bit too high, you might aggravate that.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你，如果你已经处于过度警觉状态，比如说，而你使用的频率有点太高，你可能会加剧这种情况。

sentences.en: Or you might get a little bit of a headache because it's, it's the nervous system is kind of, oh, I don't like this.
sentences.zh: 或者你可能会有点头痛，因为这是，神经系统在说，哦，我不喜欢这个。

sentences.en: So it will react.
sentences.zh: 所以它会做出反应。

sentences.en: It will, this is the way it's telling you.
sentences.zh: 它会，这就是它告诉你的方式。

sentences.en: I don't like, I don't like what I'm seeing.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢，我不喜欢我所看到的。

sentences.en: I need you, I need you to change the frequency.
sentences.zh: 我需要你，我需要你改变频率。

sentences.en: It's short-lived though, right?
sentences.zh: 不过它是短暂的，对吧？

sentences.en: Because a single session maybe lasts up to about 48 hours or something, something like this, you know, so, which, which is also the downside of neurofeedback in some ways, I guess,
sentences.zh: 因为单次疗程可能持续长达48小时左右，或者类似的情况，你知道，所以，这也是神经反馈在某些方面的缺点，我想，

sentences.en: is you need quite a few sessions.
sentences.zh: 就是你需要相当多的疗程。

sentences.en: The recommended is a minimum of 20 sessions, at least once a week, ideally two to three times a week, again, depending on your, like, how,
sentences.zh: 建议至少进行20次疗程，每周至少一次，理想情况下每周两到三次，同样，取决于你的，比如，如何，

sentences.en: how well you respond or how sensitive you are to the, to the feedback.
sentences.zh: 你反应得有多好，或者你对反馈有多敏感。

sentences.en: If you have an adverse effect, it would be short-lived and you can, and you can also, so let's say if I have a client that has, gets a headache in the session,
sentences.zh: 如果你有不良反应，它是短暂的，而且你也可以，所以假设如果我有一个客户在疗程中头痛，

sentences.en: I can just change the placement and then I stop the headache.
sentences.zh: 我可以改变放置位置，然后我就能停止头痛。

sentences.en: Um, I've, I've, I've had people, you know, almost migraine, right, onset migraine, and then we go in, put our, our, our, our instabilities over the ears, right,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我，我，我遇到过，你知道，几乎是偏头痛，对吧，偏头痛发作，然后我们进去，把我们的，我们的，我们的不稳定性放在耳朵上，对吧，

sentences.en: the left and the right ear, um, and then migraine gone, um, to the point where, you know, after, like I said, after every session, you need to check in.
sentences.zh: 左耳和右耳，嗯，然后偏头痛就消失了，嗯，以至于，你知道，正如我所说，每次疗程后，你需要进行检查。

sentences.en: And so here I am checking in a little bit earlier with this client saying, you know, how's, you know, how's the, how's the, how's the migraine?
sentences.zh: 所以现在我提前一点和这位客户检查，说，你知道，怎么样，你知道，偏头痛怎么样？

sentences.en: And they go, oh, I'd completely forgotten about it.
sentences.zh: 他们说，哦，我完全忘记了。

sentences.en: You know, so it can, it can really.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以它真的可以。

sentences.en: Yeah, that, I mean, that's what got us talking about neurofeedback in the DMs, because I'd shared that my son has migraines and he's nine and he's had them for years.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，这就是让我们在私信中谈论神经反馈的原因，因为我分享过我儿子有偏头痛，他九岁，而且他已经患病多年了。

sentences.en: And you're like, have you ever tried neurofeedback?
sentences.zh: 然后你说，你试过神经反馈吗？

sentences.en: And I was like, well, no, I haven't.
sentences.zh: 我说，嗯，没有，我没试过。

sentences.en: And then you were like, oh, I'm trained in it.
sentences.zh: 然后你说，哦，我受过这方面的培训。

sentences.en: Um, so yeah, like, I guess the disadvantage to this is, is that because it's not really available on, uh,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以是的，就像，我想这方面的缺点是，因为它目前在NHS上并不是真正可用的，

sentences.en: on the NHS currently is that if you're needing multiple sessions a week or certainly weekly, the cost can, can stack up, can't it?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你需要每周多次疗程，或者至少每周一次，成本可能会累积起来，不是吗？

sentences.en: I have found that, um, that I, as a private practitioner, um, in own therapy, I have, I think I'm, I can't remember which insurance company it is now,
sentences.zh: 我发现，嗯，我，作为一名私人执业者，嗯，在自己的治疗中，我有，我想我，我不记得是哪家保险公司了，

sentences.en: but they have allowed the neurofeedback simply because it was the last port of course.
sentences.zh: 但他们允许进行神经反馈，仅仅因为它已经是最后的手段了。

sentences.en: I had a particular patient where done loads of therapy, done all the medication, quote unquote, none of it worked.
sentences.zh: 我有一个特定的病人，做了大量的治疗，服用了所有的药物，所谓的，都没有用。

sentences.en: Let's try neurofeedback.
sentences.zh: 让我们试试神经反馈。

sentences.en: And then the insurance company goes fine.
sentences.zh: 然后保险公司说好吧。

sentences.en: So, so something is happening in terms of the recognition of this.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以关于这种认可，正在发生一些变化。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And obviously not to share any personal details of that client, but is that making progress?
sentences.zh: 显然不能分享该客户的任何个人详细信息，但它有进展吗？

sentences.en: Is it making changes for that client?
sentences.zh: 它对那个客户有改变吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Um, I don't know if I can share.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道我能不能分享。

sentences.en: I don't think they would mind.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他们会在意。

sentences.en: I mean, there's, um, an anger and difficulty almost, you know, coming in with a black eye from a, a road rage incident.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有，嗯，一种愤怒和困难，几乎是，你知道，因为路怒事件带着黑眼圈进来。

sentences.en: And, um, a few weeks later coming back into therapy saying, oh, uh, I had, there was an incident, but I wasn't bothered.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，几周后回到治疗中说，哦，嗯，我有一个，发生了一个事件，但我没被困扰。

sentences.en: And that's, yeah, some of the literature I'd been reading was,
sentences.zh: 而且那是，是的，我读过的一些文献是，

sentences.en: was kind of using neurofeedback post-traumatic brain injury and how you could really help the brain to repair itself in a way that just hasn't been possible with kind of rehab work.
sentences.zh: 是关于在创伤性脑损伤后使用神经反馈，以及你如何真正帮助大脑以一种康复工作无法实现的方式进行自我修复。

sentences.en: And it's just fascinating stuff.
sentences.zh: 这真是令人着迷的东西。

sentences.en: Mm, it really is fascinating.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它确实令人着迷。

sentences.en: And, and, and, you know, when you, when you read this list of things that it can, it can, it can help with your life.
sentences.zh: 而且，而且，而且，你知道，当你，当你阅读这个它可以帮助你生活的清单时。
